Norovirus Outbreak Impacts Retail Workforce Across Guernsey

A norovirus outbreak affecting retail sites across Guernsey is causing mounting disruption for the island’s retailers, with staff shortages, temporary closures, and operational challenges reported by several major chains and independent stores. The outbreak, which began last week, has particularly impacted St Peter Port and St Sampson, according to the Guernsey Retail Guild.

As of Wednesday, at least 18 retail sites, including supermarkets, clothing outlets, and specialty shops, have reported confirmed cases among employees. The Guernsey Health and Safety Authority has advised all retailers to implement enhanced hygiene protocols and staggered staffing to prevent further spread.

“We’re seeing absenteeism rates of up to 35% in some of our stores,” said Louise Martel, Operations Director at Channel Isles Retail. “It’s putting a lot of pressure on remaining staff, and in some locations we’ve had to close early or restrict customer access to certain sections of the store.” The company, which operates five supermarkets and six convenience stores across the island, has moved to daily deep cleans and is rotating staff to minimize contact.

Independent shops are also feeling the effects. Victor Green, owner of Green’s Shoes in St Peter Port, said, “Three of my six employees are off sick. We’re running on a skeleton crew and had to close for a full day on Monday to disinfect the shop.”

The Guernsey Retail Guild has issued guidance to members on managing sick leave and supporting staff wellbeing, urging retailers to avoid penalizing absences due to illness. “The health and safety of workers is our top priority,” said Guild President Jane Le Page. “We know the impact on trading is serious, but we must contain this outbreak.”

Analysts predict retail footfall will be suppressed until the outbreak subsides, with some chains reporting a 20% drop in sales since the start of the week. “It’s a significant operational challenge, but Guernsey’s retailers are working together to manage staff safety and maintain essential services,” said trade analyst Paul Dupré.

The outbreak remains ongoing, with health authorities monitoring the situation closely and retailers bracing for continued disruption in the days ahead.
